The Tenure of Kings and Magistrates is a 1649 book by the English poet and polemicist John Milton , in which he defends the right of people to execute a guilty sovereign, whether tyrannical or not.  The work appeared five times: in 1649, perhaps written during the trial of Charles I of England , with a second edition following in 1650 ("with improvements" [ 1 ] ), and twice in collections ( Works , 1697, and Complete Collection , 1698).  A final edition, revised, retitled, and presenting somewhat altered views, appeared in 1689. [ 2 ] "Milton’s case was not that Charles I was guilty as charged, but that Parliament had the right to prosecute him." [ 3 ]
